scope: Windows UI Automation semantic adapter implementation and cross-build evidence

commands.assertions: Injected Windows backend test enumerates UI Automation applications, creates opaque observation-scoped element IDs, resolves an editable control, validates current text, and applies a Unicode-safe insertion through ValuePattern. Empty or failed screencapture output is classified as typed permission evidence on the macOS seam.
Windows native backend compiles for the target architecture.
Existing macOS backend remains cross-build compatible.

commands.command: GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build -o /tmp/device-control-desktop-helper.exe ./cmd/desktop-helper && GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 go build -o /tmp/device-control-desktop-helper-darwin ./cmd/desktop-helper
commands.assertions: The lifecycle-managed helper executable compiles for Windows amd64 and macOS arm64 with the native backend seam.

assertions: The Windows backend now implements bounded UI Automation application and semantic-tree discovery rather than refusing semantic actions after pixel capture.
Element references remain opaque, lease-scoped, revision-scoped, and invalidated after text mutation.
Text actions preserve Unicode character-offset semantics by reading the current value and inserting at the requested rune position.
All native commands remain session-bound, timeout-bounded, and fail closed when UI Automation or permissions are unavailable.
Semantic text actions compare the live ValuePattern value with the observed value before insertion, rejecting stale mutations.
Application catalogs are lease-bound and expire before a stale application reference can be reused.
Semantic resolution preserves the UI Automation traversal order for deterministic ambiguous-match results.
Semantic assertions invalidate their observation cache after the checked operation, preventing accidental reuse of an old control reference.
limitations: No Windows host is available here; this receipt proves implementation and cross-compilation only, not NAT-03 or the Windows support row.
UI Automation behavior, elevation boundaries, IME, and permission recovery still require the live Windows fixture journey.
